source: Grokking the Advanced System Design Interview.pdf

prompt.html:
Chubby exports a file system interface similar to POSIX but simpler. It consists of a strict tree of files and directories in the usual way, with name components separated by slashes.

File format: /ls/chubby_cell/directory_name/.../file_name

Where refers to the lock service, designating that this is part of the /ls Chubby system, and is the name of a particular instance of a chubby_cell Chubby system (the term cell is used in Chubby to denote an instance of the system). This is followed by a series of directory names culminating in a . file_name

A special name,, will be resolved to the most local cell relative to /ls/local the calling application or service.

Chubby was originally designed as a lock service, such that every entity in it will be a lock. But later, its creators realized that it is useful to associate a small amount of data with each entity. Hence, each entity in Chubby can be used for locking or storing a small amount of data or both, i.e., storing small files with locks.

We can divide Chubby APIs into following groups:

General

File

Locking

Sequencer

General #

1.: Opens a given named file or directory and returns a handle. Open()

2.: Closes an open handle. Close()

3.: Allows a client to cancel all Chubby calls made by other Poison() threads without fear of deallocating the memory being accessed by them.

4.: Deletes the file or directory. Delete()

File #

1.: Returns (atomically) the whole file contents GetContentsAndStat() and metadata associated with the file. This approach of reading the whole file is designed to discourage the creation of large files, as it is not the intended use of Chubby.

2.: Returns just the metadata. GetStat()

3.: Returns the contents of a directory – that is, names and ReadDir() metadata of all children.

4.: Writes the whole contents of a file (atomically). SetContents()

5.: Writes new access control list information SetACL()

Locking #

1.: Acquires a lock on a file. Acquire()

2.: Tries to acquire a lock on a file; it is a non-blocking TryAquire() variant of Acquire.

3.: Releases a lock. Release()

Sequencer #

1.: Get the sequencer of a lock. A sequencer is a string GetSequencer() representation of a lock.

2.: Associate a sequencer with a handle. SetSequencer()

3.: Check whether a sequencer is valid. CheckSequencer() Chubby does not support operations like append, seek, move files between directories, or making symbolic or hard links. Files can only be completely read or completely written/overwritten. This makes it practical only for storing very small files.
